question: The local and the published copies of this PNG have different pixels (or the comparison could not decide). Which copy should win? Answer ours-newer when the published image is the shot we last submitted and the local one is our newer replacement, so keeping local is right. Answer contributor when the published image came from someone else (a contributor's shot, possibly pulled in by a sync), so keeping local would revert their work. Answer unclear when the evidence cannot settle it (a 16-bit PNG, color metadata the decode cannot compare, or a published image that matches an older shot of ours rather than the last one we submitted) and a human must look at both.

file.description: the PNG's path in the extension

pixels.description: decoded-pixel comparison of local against published

history.description: which commit in our history, if any, has the published pixels

context.description: anything else known: who changed the image, when, and why

inputs.context: The user replaced all six screenshots and the icon in this session and committed them before shipping; published 4.0K, local 48K, normalized hashes differ.
The user updated this screenshot that morning; three other images in the same extension were only recompressed by CI.
The published image matches no version in our history, and nothing else says who made it: it could be a contributor's shot or one of ours that was never committed.
